Every parser in `dbparser` returns a `dvobject`: a named list of tibbles
(DrugBank's are nested in lists by section) and a `source_metadata` record.
This page lists, for each parser, the tables it returns, their columns and
column types, the keys the parser checks, and the source record.

Nothing on this page is typed by hand. Each section runs the parser on the
small example files bundled with the package (`inst/extdata`) when the page is
built, and reads the tables, columns and types from the result. Row counts are
those of the example files, not of the full databases.

```{r helpers}
library(dbparser)

example_file <- function(...) {
  system.file("extdata", ..., package = "dbparser")
}

# every data frame in a dvobject, with its path, rows and typed columns
describe_dvobject <- function(x, prefix = "") {
  if (is.data.frame(x)) {
    types <- vapply(x, function(column) class(column)[1], character(1))
    return(data.frame(
      table   = prefix,
      rows    = NROW(x),
      columns = paste0("`", names(x), "` (", types, ")", collapse = ", "),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
  }
  if (is.list(x) && length(x) > 0L) {
    parts <- lapply(names(x), function(name) {
      describe_dvobject(x[[name]],
                        if (prefix == "") name else paste0(prefix, "$", name))
    })
    return(do.call(rbind, parts))
  }
  NULL
}

show_structure <- function(x) {
  knitr::kable(describe_dvobject(x), row.names = FALSE)
}

show_metadata <- function(x) {
  metadata <- get_source_metadata(x)
  fields   <- setdiff(names(metadata), "files")
  values   <- vapply(fields, function(field) {
    value <- as.character(metadata[[field]][1])
    if (is.na(value)) "NA" else value
  }, character(1))
  print(knitr::kable(data.frame(field = fields, value = values,
                                row.names = NULL)))
  cat("\n\nFiles read, with their SHA-256 hashes:\n\n")
  print(knitr::kable(metadata$files[[1]], row.names = FALSE))
}

unzip_dir <- tempfile("dbparser_structures_")
```

The `source_metadata` fields are the same for every parser. Fields the source
does not state, or that the caller did not pass (such as `retrieved_at`), are
`NA`; nothing is guessed. They are read with `get_source_metadata()`.

## DrugBank: `parseDrugBank()`

The drug records of the DrugBank XML, grouped in lists: `drugs` (always),
and with their options `salts`, `products`, `references` (articles, books,
links and attachments, for drugs and for carriers, enzymes, targets and
transporters) and `cett` (carriers, enzymes, targets and transporters, with
their polypeptides and actions). Here every option is on, on the bundled
small-molecule record.

The parser checks no key. Drug tables carry `drugbank_id`; CETT tables carry
`drugbank_id` and the CETT id (e.g. `target_id`).

```{r drugbank}
drugbank <- parseDrugBank(
  example_file("drugbank_record_small_molecule.xml"),
  drug_options       = drug_node_options(),
  parse_salts        = TRUE,
  parse_products     = TRUE,
  references_options = references_node_options(),
  cett_options       = cett_nodes_options())
show_structure(drugbank)
```

```{r drugbank-metadata, results = "asis"}
show_metadata(drugbank)
```

## OnSIDES: `parseOnSIDES()`

The seven core relational tables of OnSIDES, named after their files, and
`high_confidence` when that file is present.

The parser checks no key.

```{r onsides}
onsides <- parseOnSIDES(
  dirname(utils::unzip(system.file("onside.zip", package = "dbparser"),
                       exdir = file.path(unzip_dir, "onsides"))[1]))
show_structure(onsides)
```

```{r onsides-metadata, results = "asis"}
show_metadata(onsides)
```

## TWOSIDES: `parseTWOSIDES()`

The drug-drug interaction signals of TWOSIDES, one table.

The parser checks no key.

```{r twosides}
twosides <- parseTWOSIDES(
  utils::unzip(system.file("twoside_raw.zip", package = "dbparser"),
               exdir = file.path(unzip_dir, "twosides")))
show_structure(twosides)
```

```{r twosides-metadata, results = "asis"}
show_metadata(twosides)
```

## HPO: `parseHPO()`

Human Phenotype Ontology gene-phenotype associations as distributed by
Harmonizome, with one row per gene and one per phenotype in the lookup
tables.

The parser checks no key; `associations` holds distinct rows.

```{r hpo}
hpo <- parseHPO(example_file("hpo_gene_attribute_edges.txt"))
show_structure(hpo)
```

```{r hpo-metadata, results = "asis"}
show_metadata(hpo)
```

## HGNC: `parseHGNC()`

The HGNC complete set (`gene`), every symbol and name of each gene
(`gene_name`) and the withdrawn entries (`withdrawn`).

The parser stops unless `hgnc_id` is set and unique in `gene`. On the example
files:

```{r hgnc}
hgnc <- parseHGNC(example_file("hgnc", "hgnc_complete_set.txt"),
                  withdrawn_path = example_file("hgnc", "withdrawn.txt"))
c(gene_hgnc_id_unique         = !anyDuplicated(hgnc$gene$hgnc_id),
  gene_name_ids_are_genes     = all(hgnc$gene_name$hgnc_id %in%
                                      hgnc$gene$hgnc_id))
show_structure(hgnc)
```

```{r hgnc-metadata, results = "asis"}
show_metadata(hgnc)
```

## Health Canada DPD: `parseHealthCanadaDPD()`

The 13 tables of Health Canada's read-me. Every table except
`inactive_products` holds the rows of each product set requested, with
`extract` naming the set.

The parser stops unless `drug_code` is unique in `drug_product` and every
other table's `drug_code` is a product. On the example files:

```{r dpd}
dpd <- parseHealthCanadaDPD(example_file("health_canada_dpd"))
c(drug_product_drug_code_unique = !anyDuplicated(dpd$drug_product$drug_code),
  every_drug_code_is_a_product  = all(vapply(
    setdiff(names(dpd), "drug_product"),
    function(table) all(dpd[[table]]$drug_code %in% dpd$drug_product$drug_code),
    logical(1))))
show_structure(dpd)
```

```{r dpd-metadata, results = "asis"}
show_metadata(dpd)
```

## openFDA: `parseOpenFDA()`

One table per record level of the Drugs@FDA (`drugsfda_*`) and NDC directory
(`ndc_*`) downloads, field names as in the files.

The parser stops unless each table's key is unique and every row names its
parent row. The keys and parents it checks, read from the parser:

```{r openfda-keys}
specs <- dbparser:::openfda_table_specs()
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  table  = names(specs),
  key    = vapply(specs, function(spec) {
    if (is.null(spec$key)) "" else paste0("`", spec$key, "`", collapse = ", ")
  }, character(1)),
  parent = vapply(specs, function(spec) {
    if (is.null(spec$parent)) {
      ""
    } else {
      paste0(spec$parent[[2]], " (",
             paste0("`", spec$parent[[1]], "`", collapse = ", "), ")")
    }
  }, character(1)),
  row.names = NULL))
```

```{r openfda}
openfda <- parseOpenFDA(
  drugsfda_path = example_file("openfda", "drug-drugsfda-0001-of-0001.json.zip"),
  ndc_path      = example_file("openfda", "drug-ndc-0001-of-0001.json.zip"))
show_structure(openfda)
```

```{r openfda-metadata, results = "asis"}
show_metadata(openfda)
```

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
unlink(unzip_dir, recursive = TRUE)
```
